key_insight: Diffusion-DRF introduces a differentiable reward flow that lets preference signals backpropagate through a frozen video diffusion pipeline, enabling end-to-end fine-tuning without relying on non-differentiable human labels or discrete reward proxies.
problem_solved: Removes dependence on non-differentiable, label‑intensive preference signals (human annotations or learned discrete reward models) that cause bias, reward hacking, and unstable training in Text-to-Video diffusion fine-tuning.
method: Define a differentiable reward flow that maps model outputs (video latents/frames) to continuous preference gradients usable for backpropagation through diffusion denoising steps.

Fine-tune a video diffusion model (with core parameters partially frozen) by optimizing these differentiable preference gradients, combined with regularization to preserve generation quality and prevent reward hacking.
Use end-to-end gradient propagation instead of discrete preference optimisation, improving label efficiency and stability while maintaining text alignment and visual fidelity.
impact: Enables more stable, label‑efficient fine‑tuning of video diffusion models with fewer human annotations and reduced susceptibility to reward hacking—making preference-driven T2V improvements practical and reliable for researchers and practitioners.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input text → frozen diffusion model → differentiable reward flow → gradient backprop to fine-tuned layers

Illustration of failure modes: reward hacking vs stabilized training with differentiable rewards
paper_title: Diffusion-DRF: Differentiable Reward Flow for Video Diffusion Fine-Tuning
paper_authors: Yifan Wang, Yanyu Li, Sergey Tulyakov, Yun Fu, Anil Kag
